subject: GGIR - Sleep Regularity Index Calculation Question

messages.author: 7c38f73a4b85d711
messages.subject: GGIR - Sleep Regularity Index Calculation Question
parts:
Hi,

Apologies if this is a second post, I thought I posted this before but am unsure if I actually did post it or not, as I don't see it in the groups conversations. 

Onto the question, I am getting on average much smaller numbers for my sleep regularity indices, with some even going into the negatives. I find that upon visually checking the participants day-to-day sleep with the visual reports that the low/occasional negative numbers seem extreme. 

I was wondering how exactly SRI is dictating wakefulness and sleep. Are SIB outside of sleep windows considered to be sleep (number 1 in the picture)? Are individuals who wake after sleep onset (so during the sleep window period) considered to be awake or asleep (number 2 in the picture)? 

Both of these could contribute to getting lower numbers which would explain the overall lower SRI, especially compared to literature that implies that SRI is generally 80. 

Best,
Zachary

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GGIR - Sleep Regularity Index Calculation Question
parts:
Hi Zachary,

SRI in GGIR is derived from the detected rest periods (sustained inactivity bouts) and does not discriminate specifically between the main sleep window and naps. I used this approach because we do not have a robust nap detection method yet.

However, I have recently corresponded about this with Andrew Phillips (who originally proposed SRI) and I am now planning to make a few updates in the upcoming months:

  • I will add functionality to make SRI more compatible with their approach.
  • I plan to update the GGIR documentation on SRI to better clarify the differences.

Thanks,

Vincent
